pages.text: From erectus there is enough of a mind in a band to hold a rule. Press $(k:hominin_evolution.social) and choose $(l)Culture$(): every way your people could live by, and which they do.$(br2)None of them is simply good. Each pays off in one kind of time and costs in another.

Most only bind in the times they are about. $(l)Hard times$() are a dry season or a dry day; $(l)plenty$() is a prosperous season. The tab shows which of yours bind right now.$(br2)Letting a rule go takes the band two days, and it still binds while it fades. Once gone, it cannot come back for a day.

$(l)Our dead stay with us$() - always. You eat of the dead together, every time.$(br2)$(l)It's okay not to share when times are tight$() - in hard times they ask for less and forgive unmet wants, but keep their own food close.

$(l)Stealing is wrong when there isn't much$() - in hard times thieves are stopped and made to give it back. Take food from a hungry member yourself and the band sees it.$(br2)$(l)Stealing is wrong even in plenty$() - the same, in a prosperous season.

$(l)Sharing is always good$() - shared meals bond more and come twice as often, but an unmet want costs double.$(br2)It cannot be held alongside the tight-times rule. Without any rule, hungry members steal now and then, and the band frays a little each time.

$(l)Nobody lords it over the rest$() - always. The band keeps its bullies in line: most fights are stopped before they start, a thief who does not care is caught like anyone else, and those who stopped caring come round sooner.$(br2)It makes $(o)Shun them$() (under Social) far more likely to work: they bend, or they walk away for good.

$(l)We don't betray our own.$() In hard times far fewer in the band steal from each other; and when the band's faith in you falls to 20, it holds there - 20 more to wear through first (tribe stats show it as +20). It does not come back until it has been worn right through.

$(l)The Pile.$() A culture. When something matters - a birth, a new roof, a new ally - lay the best thing you carry on the Pile before the next night is out: +8 cohesion each, -12 if nothing goes on. Only what is hard to give up is taken, and nothing comes back off it. The first time, sneak-use the ground on your own ground with something worth it: the Pile starts there.

A desperate band may one day creep in at night and take from the Pile. Their standing with you falls through the floor, and your band never forgets it: going after them - raids, demands - is something the band is glad of.$(br2)Other bands have $(l)ways of life$() too (The others: $(o)Their way of life$()). Ways you share warm them to you; different ones they do not mind - until they want a reason.

$(l)The Feast.$() A culture. When something big happens - ready to become something new, a band of a people's size, a great weapon, the first great beast - the band feasts, two days later. Until then everyone gathers: food to piles by the fire, meat hung on racks, racks put up over fire pits, the fires fed.

When the feast begins, come to the fire: your hunger is forgotten, and everyone eats their fill - of what was gathered, and of what they carry. After it everyone is $(l)full$(): hunger falls a quarter as fast for a day and a half. Cohesion +4, and every bond grows - and a close band steals and fights far less.

Take up $(l)the Pile$() and you choose where it stands. On a $(l)stone outcrop$() every gift pulls the band closer; on the $(l)highest ground$() near you every gift makes your presence felt. Things can be taken back off it - but everyone sees you do it.
